an answer or as evidence, or in a manner analogous to
both. Hubbard v.Child,14 Jurist,545. It is here
taken as an affidavit, see Ante. In Hubbard v.Child,
the defendant, an Executor, made an affidavit on the su-
ject of the account. The account was ordered, but costs
reserved. The inference is, on this latter, that it
would be clearly regular for the Court here to reserve
costs, in making an Order for a reference. And so it
seemed to be conceded, provided a proper case was made
on the affidavits for reserving costs. Gooderh v.De
Grassi, not yet reported, where the costs were reserved,
the mortgagee had received rents and profits, sufficient
to have paid off the mortgage.
These appear to be all the cases as yet decided, which
can be of any service in throwing light upon the construc-
tion to be given to the New Orders here.
